title: Recap and decision documentation
objective: Rewrite 'everyone loved it and we're ready for rollout' into an evidence-based recap.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: Recaps and decision logs are the record of what was actually agreed. Write them precisely, and keep internal judgments separate.

items: **Customer-facing recap:** purpose, priorities, evidence, decisions, open items, and actions.
**Internal record:** qualification judgments, scores, and restricted process information. Glean's opportunity workbook is an example of an internal record.

blocks.x: Keep versions and ownership clear for every artifact.

blocks.x: When the scope is revised, point to the version used in the value model and the validation criteria. This keeps the numbers and the scope consistent.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: Don't overstate tentative agreement or expose internal scores. Verify recipients and access permissions before sharing. A draft does not authorize sending.
The customer recap and the internal record serve different readers. Keep both, and keep them consistent.

blocks.title: Two kinds of record
blocks.alt: A comparison of the customer-facing recap and the internal record. The recap confirms decisions, commitments, and next steps in customer language. The internal record adds evidence levels, risks, and open questions for the account team.
